\chapter{Which One: the Ordinals}
\label{ch:fa-ordinals}
\hlchaptermodality{20}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say first, second, third and fourth, build the ordinal of any number I can count to, and write two of them from memory.}

One borrowed ordinal at the head of the series, one ending that makes all the rest, and the two forms whose letters chapter 15 already gave.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[avval]{\fa{اول} — first, and the one ordinal Persian did not build}

\label{lesson:FA-C20-avval}



\begin{quote}
Read \textbf{\fa{۱}}, \textbf{\fa{۵}} and \textbf{\fa{۱۰}}, then say \textbf{yek}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know first — one word}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\fa{اول}} — \emph{avval} — \textbf{first}
\end{quote}

Counting says \emph{how many}. Ordering says \emph{which one}, and a floor number, a date on a notice, a chapter heading and a queue all need the second.

Three letters — \textbf{\fa{ا}}, \textbf{\fa{و}}, \textbf{\fa{ل}} — and every one of them was taught in the script chapter, so this is the third word in the book you can write from memory without meeting a new sign.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اول}} is Arabic, from the root \textbf{ʾ-w-l}. Persian did not build it from \emph{yek}.

Every other ordinal in the language \emph{is} built from its own number, as the next lesson shows. So the series opens with a borrowed word and continues with native ones — the same shape English has in \textbf{first} and \textbf{second}, which are not built from \emph{one} and \emph{two} either, before \textbf{third}, \textbf{fourth}, \textbf{fifth} fall into line.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \textbf{avval} — first
  \item \emph{Write it:} \textbf{\fa{اول}} — alef, vâv, lam
  \item \emph{Contrast:} \emph{yek} counts, \textbf{\fa{اول}} orders
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%D8\%A7\%D9\%88\%D9\%84}{Wiktionary: \fa{اول}}; \href{https://www.omniglot.com/language/numbers/persian.htm}{Omniglot, Numbers in Persian}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dovvom sevvom]{\fa{دوم} and \fa{سوم} — second, third, and one ending}

\label{lesson:FA-C20-dovvom-sevvom}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{avval}, and where it came from. Then say \textbf{do} and \textbf{se}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know first — two words and a rule}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\fa{دوم}} — \emph{dovvom} — \textbf{second}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\fa{سوم}} — \emph{sevvom} — \textbf{third}
\end{quote}

\textbf{The rule is one ending: \fa{ـم}, \emph{-om}, on the cardinal.} \emph{do} + \emph{-om} $\to$ \emph{dovvom}; \emph{se} + \emph{-om} $\to$ \emph{sevvom}. The consonant doubles at the join, which is the only thing you have to hear.

\textbf{\fa{سوم}} is written \textbf{\fa{س}}\fa{،} \textbf{\fa{و}}\fa{،} \textbf{\fa{م}} — three letters, all yours from the script chapter. That makes it the fourth word in this book you can write unaided, after \emph{se}, \emph{noh} and \emph{avval}, whose written forms the script chapter already gave.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \textbf{dovvom} — second; \textbf{sevvom} — third
  \item \emph{Split:} \emph{do} + \emph{-om}, \emph{se} + \emph{-om}
  \item \emph{Write it:} \textbf{\fa{سوم}} — sin, vâv, mim
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%D8\%B3\%D9\%88\%D9\%85}{Wiktionary: \fa{سوم}}; \href{https://www.omniglot.com/language/numbers/persian.htm}{Omniglot, Numbers in Persian}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[chahârom]{\fa{چهارم} — fourth, with nothing bending}

\label{lesson:FA-C20-chaharom}



\begin{quote}
Say the ordinal ending, then \textbf{dovvom} and \textbf{sevvom}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know first — one word}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\fa{چهارم}} — \emph{chahârom} — \textbf{fourth}
\end{quote}

\emph{chahâr} + \emph{-om}, and nothing happens at the join. \emph{panjom}, \textquotedblleft{}fifth,\textquotedblright{} is the same: the cardinal ends in a consonant, so the ending simply follows it.

\emph{dovvom} and \emph{sevvom} doubled a consonant only because their cardinals end in a vowel. Two and three are the exception; four onwards is the rule, all the way up. \emph{dahom} is \textquotedblleft{}tenth\textquotedblright{}, \emph{bistom} is \textquotedblleft{}twentieth\textquotedblright{}, \emph{sadom} is \textquotedblleft{}hundredth.\textquotedblright{}

So a reader who has twelve cardinals and one ending has twelve ordinals, minus the borrowed first.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \textbf{chahârom} — fourth
  \item \emph{Build:} \emph{panj} + \emph{-om} $\to$ \textbf{panjom}, fifth
  \item \emph{Build:} \emph{dah} + \emph{-om} $\to$ \textbf{dahom}, tenth
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%DA\%86\%D9\%87\%D8\%A7\%D8\%B1\%D9\%85}{Wiktionary: \fa{چهارم}}; \href{https://www.omniglot.com/language/numbers/persian.htm}{Omniglot, Numbers in Persian}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Payoff — which one}

\label{lesson:FA-C20-practice}



\begin{quote}
Count one to twenty, then read \textbf{\fa{۷}}, \textbf{\fa{۱۲}} and \textbf{\fa{۱۰۰}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item Say the first four in order, then out of order.
  \item \textbf{Build}, do not recall: fifth, seventh, tenth, twentieth, hundredth, from the cardinals and the ending.
  \item Say which one of the whole series is not built that way, and where it came from.
  \item Write \textbf{\fa{اول}} and \textbf{\fa{سوم}} from memory. Both are made entirely of letters the script chapter taught.
  \item Use one: name the floor a room is on, and the day of the month a notice gives.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.omniglot.com/language/numbers/persian.htm}{Omniglot, Numbers in Persian}.
\end{tcolorbox}
